items.title: Item A: New Hampshire not acquired from its authoritative filing universe
items.summary: NH's candidate population is still PILOT_DERIVED, not migrated to the state's authoritative candidate-filing source. The SOS filing PDF is retrieved and hashed but its pages are rotated, so the generic table layer returns ZERO_ROWS, and there is no sourced crosswalk from an NH district to an OCD division. A prototype recovered 1,268 rows whose segmentation could not be verified and was not shipped.
evidence: docs/owner-audit/session-c.md:687 (Item A acceptance row, New Hampshire — NOT ACQUIRED)
docs/frontier.md:774-780 ("The two corpora that are retrieved and not normalized")

items.title: Item A: New Jersey not acquired from its authoritative filing universe
items.summary: NJ's candidate population is still PILOT_DERIVED. NJ's Division of Elections files federal office only; the state's true universe is the union of that authority and 21 county clerks, so no single acquisition could earn the word "statewide". Population is honestly relabelled but not migrated.
evidence: docs/owner-audit/session-c.md:688 (Item A acceptance row, New Jersey — NOT ACQUIRED, and could not be)

items.title: Item K: production Ask model is claude-opus-5, not the directive-required claude-sonnet-5
items.summary: The Sonnet 5 switch was made, measured, and reverted the same day under RULING 234's own reversibility clause — a correct use of the mechanism — but the directive's final acceptance requires production serving claude-sonnet-5. Readers currently get claude-opus-5, so Item K cannot be called complete.
evidence: docs/owner-audit/session-c.md:865 ("Production serves the reverted model" — PENDING THE MERGE, pass = claude-opus-5)

items.title: The autonomous runner is not verified after this session's schema v3 migration broke it
items.summary: This session migrated the shared control-plane database to schema v3 from a worktree while the runner executed from the main checkout on pre-session code declaring v2. control-plane:gate refused undeclared tables, so the runner shut itself down: cycles exited NON-ZERO from ~19:56Z and digests read "0 providers, 0 units". The repair is in this merge; verification can only follow it, and until the runner is observed completing a clean cycle on the merged code, this item stays UNFINISHED.
evidence: docs/state.md:23015-23021 ("THE RUNNER, and this session broke it")

items.title: Runner auto-restart (999x / 5min) not observed to recover the process
items.summary: The Scheduled Task is configured to retry a dead runner within 5 minutes, but 31 minutes after the runner's death at ~11:56 it had still not been restarted (checked at 12:27:21), with 0 pilot-runner processes running. The root cause of the STATUS_CONTROL_C_EXIT (0xC000013A) that kills the process has not been established and is recorded as an open diagnosis rather than guessed.

items.title: Two runner mechanisms (Scheduled Task + Startup entry) is an unresolved owner decision
items.summary: Two runner processes were found writing digests 11 seconds apart, one launched by the Scheduled Task and one orphaned from a Startup entry. The duplicate process was stopped, but which single mechanism should own the runner going forward is left as an owner decision.

items.title: ~1,000 stranded occurrences from an earlier unbounded run still draining
items.summary: An earlier lane's unbounded run opened roughly 1,000 occurrences that are still open in the control plane. resumeOpenOccurrence picks them up rather than stranding them, so they drain rather than leak, but the drain happens over many cycles and is not yet complete.

items.title: Item H seeded failure 3: admin render self-check compares a number to itself
items.summary: countClaimsFor in lib/control-plane/owner-surface.ts:665 sets `stated` and `rendered` to the same expression for all four entries, so the check that is supposed to catch a number rendered without a denominator cannot ever fail. This is corrected from an earlier MET claim to NOT MET.

items.title: Item J undeclared-token sweep has no red arm — the "plant-check both ways" claim is false
items.summary: The guard asserts the current state only; it was never shown failing on a planted violation, so it cannot distinguish "the rule holds" from "the sweep looked at nothing".

items.title: Item B's documented verification command produces a SKIP, not the stated MET result
items.summary: The row's "Where to verify" instructs `pnpm build && pnpm start` then the render test, but plain `next start` carries no `--import ./scripts/trap-outbound.mjs` and no WTP_OUTBOUND_LOG. An owner following the row verbatim gets a skip and exit 0, not the recorded pass.

items.title: Item 5a is not named anywhere in the acceptance package or the orchestration plan
items.summary: The orchestration plan names its Lane C workstream "Items 5b to 5e" and nothing on disk names a 5a. The package does not resolve whether Item 5 had a first part; the integration owner must either name 5a and its verification, or state that Item 5 begins at 5b.

items.title: Item 5: enrichment/local-jurisdiction obligations never materialized into work state
items.summary: The two new scheduler providers (candidate-enrichment, local-jurisdictions) schedule correctly, but the committed shadow store holds 405 obligations split only between meetings (370) and campaign-finance (35) — zero candidate-enrichment rows and zero local-jurisdiction rows. `pnpm freshness:shadow` would materialize them but was not run because it writes and cannot run from an audit.

items.title: Item E: run-provenance proof class remains SESSION_MEASURED, not upgraded
items.summary: proofClassOf requires runClass != LOCAL_SESSION, a clean working tree, and integratedAtRunTime. This run records LOCAL_SESSION/true/false. A session cannot award itself independence by running the same command twice; moving the proof class needs a CI or scheduled run on an already-merged SHA.

items.title: Item F: legacy-host 301 redirect is PENDING THE MERGE
items.summary: netlify.toml's redirect ships with the RULING-1 merge, so it cannot serve before it. Measured before the change on 2026-09-01, sparkwtp.netlify.app returned 200 (serving the app in parallel), not a redirect. Must be re-run after the merge; a 301 to meanwhileusa.com is the pass.

items.title: Item H: admin control centre is MET in tree/provider but NOT YET LIVE
items.summary: middleware.ts, which enforces admin-host routing, ships with the RULING-1 merge, so until that merge admin.meanwhileusa.com serves the public app rather than the admin surface. Must be re-verified with the HTTPS probe after the merge.

items.title: Item K: production serving the reverted model is PENDING THE MERGE
items.summary: Requires the deploy to verify. After the merge, POST to /api/ask/grounded with the synthetic-run header must read trace.synthesis.model = claude-opus-5 (medium) — the revert target. Anything else, or a null model, is a fail.

items.title: Item I: staging database isolation not met — no Neon API key available
items.summary: There is no Neon control-plane API key available, so a database branch cannot be created for staging. Nothing pretends isolation exists; the seeded-failure check confirms production DATABASE_URL is REFUSED (not silently used) in a branch-deploy context.

items.title: Item I: staging branch named "test" not "staging" (RULING 233 conflict)
items.summary: Netlify derives a branch deploy's hostname as <branch>.<suffix>, so RULING 233's branch name "staging" and host "test.meanwhileusa.com" cannot both hold. RULING 235 records this as a FACT without amending the ruling (a session cannot legislate). The choice is carried to the owner as tracker row NH304.

items.title: Item I: Netlify Deploy Previews remain cancelled since g17, contrary to the brief
items.summary: The brief says Deploy Previews "remain available"; they have been cancelled since an earlier session (g17). Left cancelled, and the conflict is represented in netlify.toml rather than resolved, because re-enabling would amend a ruling.

items.title: Item J: dark-theme mark/State-tab color adjacency — owner decision
items.summary: In dark theme, --mark and the selected State tab render the exact same hex (#00b894). The lane's read is that they do not visually collapse, but no adjustment was made because the brief reserved this judgement to the owner. Six comparison captures are provided.

items.title: Item J: B01 (settle the product's name) open 21 days, brand work shipped anyway
items.summary: B01 ("settle the product's name") has been in the Needs-Sean queue 21 days. The audit states a brand item shipped while that row is open is a decision the package cannot make on its own.

items.title: Item H: owner must retrieve WTP_ADMIN_SECRET from the Netlify UI to log in
items.summary: WTP_ADMIN_SECRET was generated and set via the Netlify API without ever being printed anywhere. The owner must read its value from Site configuration -> Environment variables to log into the admin control centre, or replace it with one of their own.

items.title: OWN01 (WGH-20): body-count mismatch does not reproduce; needs the owner's original capture
items.summary: The Who Governs Here panel reports 9 and renders 9 at 85641, from one derivation, so there is no second source to reconcile a 7-vs-6 mismatch against. The owner's row is PENDING with no screenshot; what is needed is the capture the owner saw, or the address and date that produced it.

items.title: OWN05 (BAL-36): no legislative-record source for the governor; needs approval
items.summary: No adapter anywhere in lib/sources/ covers executive action records (bills signed, vetoed, executive orders), so Ask can only answer as a gap. Adding an external source is on CLAUDE.md's ask-before list; the owner must approve adding one and choose the publisher (Secretary of State bill history, Governor's office, or another).

items.title: OWN06 (BAL-37): no address autocomplete; needs source approval + privacy call
items.summary: The Census geocoder used has no typeahead endpoint, and suggesting from held partial data would silently exclude unheld addresses. The owner must approve adding an address-suggestion source and decide whether partial addresses may leave the product as the reader types.

items.title: Drive mirror refused to overwrite repo-inventory.md; owner must decide
items.summary: The mirror guard refused an overwrite because the Drive copy of docs/repo-inventory.md carries two lines matching no git revision of the file. Diagnosis shows they are a stale generation's header/count stamp, mirrored but never committed, not any owner edit. The guard was correct to refuse; the owner must choose to refresh the mirror from the committed file or keep the older generation.

items.title: NH303: four full-resolution AZCC portrait originals staged, awaiting owner
items.summary: Four of the nine approved portraits (Arizona Corporation Commissioners) were approved as CMS-rendition thumbnails, but removing the rendition parameters on the same host returns 2,533-3,275px originals. They are staged, not shipped, because the owner approved a 133px crop, not the full-resolution file.

items.title: 65 remaining Needs-Sean tracker rows carrying decision cards
items.summary: Beyond the items individually listed above (OWN01/05/06, B01, staging isolation/branch-name, Drive mirror, admin secret), the tracker carries 65 rows overall marked NOT_MACHINE_VERIFIABLE with a decision card each, ranging from 21 days old (abuse policy, entity decision, trademark search, buyer calls, etc.) down to same-day. Each card states what is needed, the options, and their cost.

items.title: 4 Needs-Sean tracker rows need only the owner's acknowledgement, not a decision
items.summary: NS18 (Sources tab count of 2 is uncapped, just given 2), NH208 (nothing wrong with the owner's ruleset), NH212 (a serving-edge guard change), and NH08 (Newbury's Selectboard correctly shows meetings from two sources) each close the moment the owner confirms having read them.

items.title: 40 of 89 audit acceptance claims CONFIRMED_BROKEN, recorded not repaired
items.summary: A 71-agent, 10-dimension adversarial refutation pass checked 89 of this session's own acceptance claims, raised 60 as suspect, and confirmed 40 broken (20 refuters were themselves shown wrong; 0 undecided). The findings — chiefly guards that cannot catch what they are cited as catching (the --mark scope test exempting legend dots, a comment-stripping sweep skipping the directory whose comment caused the defect, derive()'s template-level continue, the NS12 predicate accepting placeholder strings, the unchecked middleware matcher, plus the Item B/H/J/E findings itemized separately above) — are open defects with evidence in the committed findings file. Repairing them is stated as a session's own future work, not done here.
evidence: docs/evidence/session-c-refutation-2026-09-01.json (claimsChecked=89, nonHoldsRaised=60, confirmedBroken=40, refuterWasWrong=20; findings[] where verdict2=="CONFIRMED_BROKEN")

items.title: No systematic "prove it looked" check is applied broadly across the project's sweeps
items.summary: Three separate instruments were found this session reporting clean results while looking at nothing (a model-comparison harness silently filtering questions, a --regenerate arm-name bug, and a stylesheet sweep blind to nested CSS), and the refutation pass then found guards with the same shape across the acceptance package. The plant-check pattern (planting a violation and asserting the guard goes red) exists for one test but is not applied broadly.

items.title: The generated-artifact test race is reduced but not eliminated
items.summary: tests/generated-artifacts.test.ts now re-derives a mismatch once, distinguishing a real drift (which reproduces) from a working-tree race (which does not) and naming the cause. A non-reproducing mismatch still throws, so it can still turn a pnpm gates run red at random. Isolating or removing the shared-tree mutation remains open.

items.title: 211 newly acquired Arizona candidates are inventory, not product — no promotion tail
items.summary: The 211 newly acquired Arizona candidates are ACQUIRED -> EXTRACTED -> NORMALIZED -> CANONICALLY_LINKED, but nothing in app/ or components/ reads data/hunt/<state>-candidate-universe-2026.json or calls projectOntoZip. Under RULING 224, an acquisition obligation does not close until a reader-facing surface reflects it or renders the honest gap; held data with no live promotion tail is a defect, retroactively.

items.title: H3 fly-in: p95-sustained frame-rate ratio fails (66.2%) though median passes
items.summary: The owner's median-ratio criterion for the zip fly-in passes at 99.7%, but the p95-sustained ratio is 66.2% and would fail under a tail-latency criterion. This is still open on ordinary (non-degraded) hardware even after the separate no-GPU-acceleration repair closed; a median-only criterion is blind to concentrated jank (app p99 frame time 61.0ms vs bare 18.4ms).

items.title: Ask: ASK-19 700-char budget still fails Q3/Q5 on the model now shipping
items.summary: Q3 and Q5 fail the 700-character synthesis budget on claude-opus-5 (now the production model again after the revert), 0 of 3 passes each, because an 18-record evidence pack cannot fit. This is a real unanswered reader question and a pipeline defect unchanged by the model switch/revert; the owed decision is whether the budget rises for large packs, packs are summarized in stages, or the budget becomes a target rather than a post-hoc gate.

items.title: Ask: the xhigh and max effort levels structurally break the JSON output contract
items.summary: At max_tokens 2048, thinking counts against the ceiling and the JSON answer truncates mid-string at the xhigh and max effort levels, making them unusable. medium is retained instead; the two levels remain broken rather than fixed or removed.

items.title: One test failed once inside pnpm gates and its name was never recorded
items.summary: A gates run recorded a real single-test ASSERTION_FAILURE (4523/4522/1) but scripts/gates.mjs at the time did not extract the failing test's name from node:test's own output, so it went unrecorded. Two subsequent full runs came back clean (4523/4523, 14/14). The fix (failingTests capture) prevents recurrence but cannot recover the original name; it is owed to reproduce under load or catch a recurrence.

items.title: Instrument debt: the gate-run record identifier collides under parallel execution
items.summary: Gate-run records are numbered from local state, so parallel branches allocated the same record numbers independently and conflicted on merge. Since RULING 190/191 make parallel lanes the default, this recurs by design; the durable fix is an identifier needing no agreement (tested SHA plus run instant), not yet built.

items.title: Instrument debt: release:freeze has no automatic path out of its own loop
items.summary: Every commit to main deploys, including the post-deploy observer's own reading, which moves production out from under the reading just taken. The session cleared the freeze loop by hand each round; no automatic exit exists yet.

items.title: Instrument debt: the gate abort-vs-real duration heuristic does not always discriminate
items.summary: The duration heuristic for telling an early-abort false-red apart from a real failure held on one tree (59s fail vs 75s pass) but failed on another (44s fail vs 43s pass). The now-recorded failureKind field is the reliable signal, but the unreliable duration heuristic itself has not been removed.

items.title: Instrument debt: the client-JS baseline for / looks stale, not re-baselined
items.summary: Measured 2003 KB against a 2653 KB baseline last set 2026-08-29. A baseline that far above the current measurement cannot catch a real regression; re-baselining was judged not this session's to do.

items.title: Arizona's source universe is larger than any one query already run
items.summary: Three GetNEWTableData filters union to 860 rows across 732 entities, 16 reachable from no other filter, and the FTP root at ftp.azsos.gov has four directories where the record said one — ElectionResults (1998-2026) was never walked. County, municipal and school-district filers whose filing officer is not the Secretary of State remain owed.

items.title: NH has 14 remaining known routes; SOS filed-report PDF series is highest-value
items.summary: 14 routes are catalogued in data/hunt/nh-remaining-routes.json. The API's reportCount is null, which is why six candidates carry REGISTERED_NO_ACTIVITY_REPORTED rather than a report-level claim; the filed-report PDFs are the materially distinct representation that could answer it.

items.title: A usable Tom Horne portrait is still owed
items.summary: The held file (Tom Headshot 60px_0.jpg) is 60px against a 96px floor, and azed.gov answers a Cloudflare interstitial to every client tried. Per RULING 206, the owed thing is another representation of the same record, not a harder fetch of the same URL. Not one of the nine owner-approved portraits — his was never among them.

items.title: The worker cost ledger still cannot see cache-read tokens (AttemptCost)
items.summary: The autonomous-worker cost digest reports cache hit rate as NOT MEASURED because nothing in AttemptCost records a cache read. Production Ask requests are separately measured at Anthropic's own usage block (15,731 cache-read tokens, 4 of 6 calls reading), but the worker cost ledger has no equivalent instrumentation.
